newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West power mostly higher, forward months jump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West power mostly higher, forward months jump.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. West were steady to stronger with forward cash months trading significantly higher, brokers and marketers said.

Western prices for November and December and even well into next year jumped significantly Tuesday, with traders citing strong natural gas prices and higher winter demand in the Northwest as giving strength.

Also, Bonneville Power Administration said it was offering firm power at prices mostly steady from Tuesday, with heavy load hours offered at $22.50, with power to the Northwest valued at $23.00 and the California-Oregon Border (COB)/Nevada Oregon Border (NOB) set at $24.50.
In the spot market, firm, peak COB power for Wednesday was said to be steady to higher in the $23.00-24.00 area from $21.50-24.50 for Tuesday delivery, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day COB power was quoted steady at $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.

November COB was assessed in the $23.00-23.50 range from discussion at $19.90-22.20 on Tuesday, while December peak COB was talked at $23.25-23.60 from $22.30 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) peak power for Wednesday delivery was talked higher in the $22.50-23.50 range from $19.00-22.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak Mid-C was said to be trading higher at $18.75-19.25 from near $16.50 on Tuesday.
November peak Mid-C was pegged at $21.75-22.50 from a Tuesday range of $20.35-20.95, the sources said.
Peak Mid-C for the first quarter of next year was pegged in the 17.50-18.50 range with one unconfirmed trade reported at $18.00 per MWh.

Peak Palo Verde (PV) power for Wednesday delivery was assessed at $21.00-24.00 from a Tuesday discussion range at $20.00-22.00, while off-peak next day PV was assessed higher at $17.00-18.00 from $14.00-16.00 per MWh on Tuesday.
November PV was talked in the $21.00-21.75 range from $20.50-20.75 on Tuesday, while December was pegged at $22.00-22.40 per MWh, the brokers and marketers said.
First quarter PV was bid at $17.85, while third quarter PV was talked at just over $25.00, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
